Nutrition! What do you like to eat (or avoid) before training? what do you eat during long runs/races? What works for you that people really look at you funny when you suggest it?

Night before a race I always have pasta or rice, boring I know.

After work outs I attempt to either have my meal or eat at least some form of protein.

During long races (half marathon or over) I take water at all aid stations and have a glucose gel of some sort every seven miles. If I'm just training I have no food, and water only when the run is over 1.5 hours.
I read somewhere that "carb loading" is somewhat of a myth/bro-science. I still do it cause it's what I've known for over 15 years, and I get to stuff my face guilt-free ;)
Yeah... and you really don't want to have too much either. I've bloated my self with a carboload the night before a race or two, not pleasant.

When I need to take a shit, coffee or a banana. Or both if I want to live dangerously.

When I'm hot, frozen applesauce pouches work great as an ice pack. When they thaw, they're a great source of fluid, sugar, and fiber.

When I want solid food on a training run, a shit burrito is pretty good. Take some whipped honey, spread it on a soft burrito/wrap, roll it up and put it in a ziplock bag. You can use peanut butter if you're not allergic to it (I am so it's whipped honey for me).

If I want to barf, anything with pomegranate flavoring. I had a bad experience one time and I just can't stomach the stuff anymore.

grenadine huh... most "cherry" flavors tend to use that.

I got the idea of hummus-tacos(burritos) from Jurek's book and they work great, so great that I "accidentally" eat them all the first half hour of the run instead of hour 2-3 like I was supposed to.
No, I like grenadine, it's the pomegranate that makes me barf. Cherry is fine. That weird seeded fruit thing isn't.

I meant to say that "grenadine" is a sweet sweet syrup made (or used to at some point) from pomegranate and is typically used in flavoring "cherry-flavored" drinks/foods.

Also, screw you, those weird seeded fruit things are delicious! or... just buy all of them out of spite and sent them this way ;)
Screw me indeed. Grenadine is made from pomegranate? Never knew that. Guess that's right up there with I like ketchup but not tomatoes.

A peanut butter and jelly sandwich for breakfast the day of the race, maybe 2 hours before start time. For training, I try to avoid eating much beforehand, maybe granola or yogurt. I prefer to take a protein shake right after the run to start recovery.

If a run is less than 2 hours then nothing. 2 hours plus I like to carry some banana pb and j wraps. Easy to eat on the go, easy on my stomach. In my experience real food is always better than gels. You just need to experiment and find what agrees with you. Never try anything new on race day.

Why are prices always X.99 instead of a whole number?
It's called psychological pricing. Basically, people think they're getting a better deal than they really are because they treat say $7.99 as $7 rather than $8.
That is the reason, but seriously, how many people still believe that? Everybody I know would say something is $8 and not $7.99.
I think you overestimate people's intelligence. Apparently enough people believe it that it's still a thing. You clearly surround yourself with smart people. :)
They should try $8.01 vs $7.99 - maybe .01 sounds cheaper :)

Pricing is also frequently used to indicate clearance levels.

Anything ending with .98 is clearance. Anything ending in .95 has been on clearance for x amount of time and has already had a further price reduction, etc.
Any item price ending in .X3 is generally as low as it will ever go - they basically want it off the fucking shelf so it will stop taking up space and they can move in more profitable product.
That depends entirely on the retailer obviously. The one I work for uses different schemes. .x8 is very common. Beyond that though...it probably varies too much to be reliable

In addition to psychological pricing which is why it's continued today, the practice became more popular with the advent of the cash register. Clerks would be forced to open the cash to provide change on the sale, thus registering the transaction.

Gas prices take it to another extreme with the 2.99 9/10ths thing. Although I thought I read something about the reasoning behind that 9/10ths thing before and I forget ... brain doesn't work as well as it once did at remembering things. Although I have to say the return to using the "10 cents more per gallon if paying credit" is some serious bullshit. I understand that credit cards have a very small additional overhead cost to the seller but it is no where near that magnitude - should be more like a single 20 cent extra fee to the customer and not per-gallon.

Back in the day, before credit cards, stores would price products X.99 so retailers would always open the cash register for change, making sure that the transaction would be accounted for and that no money was stolen. Eventually, it became standard pricing.
